**Preserve partial manifest GC stats on errors.**

Disposition after checking the current caller: `ReclaimObservedValueLogSources` returns `ValueLogGCStats`, whose counters describe the observed primary value-log sources. It has always discarded the separate leaf-GC result on both success and failure; that caller and return type are unchanged by this PR. Combining immutable manifest or leaf-segment counters into the observed-vlog counters would change their meaning, and exposing the separate result requires an API change.

The direct backend `LeafGenerationGC` API retains and returns its actual completed revision deletions with an error; the new cancellation/late-inventory regression receipts exercise that behavior. The lifecycle harness reports that separate result directly. I am declining the suggested cached-caller API expansion in this focused prerequisite; cached observed-vlog stats are not claimed to be a combined leaf/revision report.

Current source: [observed-source return type](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/blob/852aa29e1eed3511f93aba244aef917c89d033e8/TreeDB/caching/db.go#L5558), [separate leaf side call](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/blob/852aa29e1eed3511f93aba244aef917c89d033e8/TreeDB/caching/db.go#L5650), [direct backend partial-stats return](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/blob/852aa29e1eed3511f93aba244aef917c89d033e8/TreeDB/db/leaf_generation_gc.go#L92).

`@snissn` Thanks for the clarification. I withdraw this finding.

`ReclaimObservedValueLogSources` returns `ValueLogGCStats` for observed primary value-log sources, not a combined leaf/revision GC report. My suggestion conflated these separate results. Exposing `LeafGenerationGCStats` through that caller would require an API change, not a partial-stats fix.

The direct backend `LeafGenerationGC` API returns completed revision-deletion stats with an error. No cached-caller change is needed for this finding.

**🩺 Stability & Availability** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**A failed quarantine cleanup leaves `manifest.gc.*.tmp` behind and blocks all future revision GC.**

Two paths can fail after the placeholder is created: the `BeforeRename` hook and `RenameStableChildFile`. On both paths the cleanup result of `RemoveStableChildFile` is discarded. If that unlink fails, a `manifest.gc.*` placeholder stays in the directory. Every later scan then returns `ErrRecoveryRequired` at Line 130–131, but the handle is not poisoned and no error explains why. The placeholder is an empty file that this code created itself. Propagate the cleanup error, or call `s.ambiguous` when cleanup fails, so the operator sees the cause.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
 	if err := rootpublication.RenameStableChildFile(s.parent, f.name, quarantine); err != nil {
-		_ = rootpublication.RemoveStableChildFile(s.parent, quarantine)
-		return err
+		if rmErr := rootpublication.RemoveStableChildFile(s.parent, quarantine); rmErr != nil {
+			return s.ambiguous(errors.Join(err, rmErr))
+		}
+		return err
 	}
```
</details>

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid opening every manifest revision at once**

When churn has accumulated more revision files than the process open-file limit, this inventory loop keeps every file descriptor open in `files` until the entire scan returns. `OpenStableChildFile` then fails with `EMFILE` before the deletion loop begins, so `LeafGenerationGC` deletes no revisions, and every retry encounters the same failure; this is especially reachable with typical 256/1024 descriptor limits. Process revisions in bounded batches or otherwise release handles while preserving the identity/rebinding checks.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in852aa29e1. [GC now retains16 exact deletion handles plus one transient scan child](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/blob/852aa29e1eed3511f93aba244aef917c89d033e8/TreeDB/db/leaf_manifest_revision_gc.go#L71), validates the complete inventory before each batch, and repeats within one call. Fresh held/registry protection is reevaluated; initial names/digests never authorize deletion. Footprint limits remain per-inventory. [The isolated Linux regression](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/blob/852aa29e1eed3511f93aba244aef917c89d033e8/TreeDB/db/leaf_manifest_revision_gc_fd_linux_test.go#L15) reproduces old EMFILE under RLIMIT64, then deletes255 of257 revisions with2 protected. Rename-sampled descriptors12→28; later malformed inventory/cancellation retain truthful completed counts. [Between-batch held protection](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/blob/852aa29e1eed3511f93aba244aef917c89d033e8/TreeDB/db/leaf_manifest_revision_gc_fd_linux_test.go#L202) also passes. Exact independent review is CLEAN; focused normal/race/vet pass. Worst-case full rescans cost O(N²/16);32-revision smoke passes, while sustained cost acceptance remains the final lifecycle gate.

**🚀 Performance & Scalability** | **🔵 Trivial** | **🏗️ Heavy lift**

**The quadratic rescan loop holds `db.writeMu` and `db.rootReuseMu` for the whole run.**

`gcLeafManifestRevisions` takes `db.writeMu` and `db.rootReuseMu` before it calls `gcRevisionsWithHeldViews`. It releases both locks only after every batch finishes. Each batch calls `scanRevisionGCBatch`, which runs these steps on every `manifest.durable.*` entry:

- opens the file
- runs `Stat`
- reads the whole file with `io.ReadAll`
- computes `sha256.Sum256`
- decodes the file
- runs `ValidateStableChildLink`

Only 16 files are deleted per batch. With N eligible revisions, the run performs about N/16 full scans, or about N²/16 file opens and reads. Writers and snapshot admission are blocked for that whole time. The comment at Lines 111-114 documents the scan cost but not the lock scope.

`MaintenanceLimits` bounds each scan separately. It does not bound the total time the locks are held. Revisions build up under churn, which is the scenario this PR targets. Some examples:

- 2,000 revisions take about 125 scans and about 250k file reads.
- 10,000 revisions take about 625 scans and about 6.25M file reads.

Writes stall during all of that work.

Options that keep the exact-handle guarantee:
- On later scans, skip `io.ReadAll`, digest, and decode for non-pending names that are not `currentName`. Check the saved `StableIdentity` and size for those names. Full validation stays on pending candidates and on the current manifest.
- Or release `writeMu` and `rootReuseMu` between batches. Then re-capture and revalidate `RecoverableRootSet` for each batch, so later batches do not reuse stale authority.
- Or cap the number of batches per invocation and return. Callers already retry, and `pending` is rebuilt on the next run.

The total GC-owned child descriptor bound includes link validation:16 selected handles +1 scan child or quarantine placeholder +1 temporary validation child=18; existing parent/manager/process descriptors are separate. The sampled descriptor count is not a global peak. Capping batches, releasing those locks, reusing stale numeric identity or skipping full validation would change the accepted protection/completion contract, so this patch does not adopt those alternatives. Actual finite sustained D measurements remain required to qualify maintenance cost and physical retention; the descriptor repair alone does not accept capacity or latency.
